functions.name: core_watchdog_start
functions.brief: Start the independent watchdog with a timeout in milliseconds. Selects the best prescaler/reload combination automatically. Common values: 1000, 2000, 5000, 10000 (max ~28000). WARNING: Once started, the IWDG cannot be stopped, and it keeps running in Stop and Standby. core_stop_for() wakes to feed it; core_standby_for() refuses sleeps longer than half the timeout.

functions.name: core_watchdog_running
functions.brief: Returns 1 if this firmware has started the watchdog (core_watchdog_start).

functions.name: core_watchdog_sleep_chunk_ms
functions.brief: The longest a sleep may run between feeds while the watchdog runs: half its timeout, in ms. 0 when the watchdog isn't running. The RTC that times the sleep and the IWDG share the LSI, so the margin holds even when the LSI is far from nominal (the L0's is 26-56 kHz).

functions.name: core_watchdog_feed
functions.brief: Feed the watchdog. Must be called before the timeout expires. On ROM-DFU builds this also retires the brick-recovery strike counter, once, after the app has run for max(10 s, 2 x the timeout) — no call needed.

functions.name: core_watchdog_caused_reset
functions.brief: Check if the last reset was caused by the watchdog. On ROM_DFU builds, core_init() reads and clears the hardware flag early (for the strike counter), stashing the cause in reserved SRAM — so prefer that when it's valid; otherwise fall back to the raw RCC_CSR flag.

functions.name: core_watchdog_clear_flags
functions.brief: Clear all reset flags (call after checking cause).

functions.name: core_watchdog_debug_freeze
functions.brief: Freeze the IWDG while the core is halted under a debugger, so a breakpoint doesn't let the watchdog reset the chip out from under an SWD session. Firmware-side so it holds for any probe/toolchain (rev b exposes SWD on L4).

functions.name: ll_iwdg_init
functions.brief: Initialize and start the independent watchdog. prescaler: LL_IWDG_PSC_* value reload:    reload value (0-4095) WARNING: Once started, the IWDG cannot be stopped. The only way to disable it is a full MCU reset. Make sure your main loop calls ll_iwdg_refresh() regularly. The LSI oscillator is automatically started when IWDG is enabled.

functions.name: ll_iwdg_refresh
functions.brief: Refresh (feed) the watchdog. Call this periodically in your main loop to prevent a watchdog reset.

functions.name: ll_iwdg_caused_reset
functions.brief: Check if the last reset was caused by the IWDG. Call early in main() to detect watchdog resets.

functions.name: ll_rcc_clear_reset_flags
functions.brief: Clear the reset flags (so the next check gives a fresh result). Clears all reset flags, not just IWDG.
